analysis.title: The Strong Outlook for Liquid Alternatives: Why GMO Is Allocating Multi-Asset Portfolios to Liquid Alts Today
key_insights: GMO describes its outlook for liquid alternative strategies as unusually strong and has used liquid alts in multi-asset portfolios for over 25 years.
GMO uses liquid alts as dry powder to redeploy when valuations are favorable. The asset class can also earn an outsized allocation when other opportunities are underwhelming.
Positive cash rates help liquid alts, which seek returns over cash.

Equity valuation spreads are wider than normal across regions and styles (U.S. vs. Europe, semiconductors vs. industrials). Most liquid alts take long-short relative value positions, so wide spreads widen the opportunity set.

Mutual funds can now replicate hedge fund results within defined risk parameters. Banks offer prime-broker-like services, liquid derivatives and exchange-traded strategies have expanded the long and short universe, and basket swaps allow customized short selection.
Hedge fund strategies historically charged 2% management and 20% performance fees, often with no hurdle. GMO says strategies with competitive fee structures are now available.
GMO prefers liquid alts over credit, where spreads remain historically tight, and over expensive stocks.
GMO sees an elevated risk of an unwind in the AI trade. ALTA is not a tail-risk hedge but is managed for low equity correlation and should perform well in an AI unwind, according to GMO.

ALTA's largest risk allocations are long-short strategies shorting the frothiest parts of the AI ecosystem, quality long-short positions that tend to be defensive in equity drawdowns, and global macro exposure that is net short equities.
Global Asset Allocation Strategy (65/35 benchmark) holds 17% in ALTA. Benchmark-Free Allocation Strategy holds 30% in alts, including 13% in ALTA, plus Equity Dislocation and Emerging FX.

sector_views.rationale: ALTA's long-short strategies short the frothiest parts of the AI ecosystem, and GMO sees elevated risk of an AI trade unwind.
GMO prefers liquid alts to credit because spreads are still historically tight.

trade_ideas.description: Allocate to liquid alternatives (GMO Alternative Allocation Strategy, ALTA) instead of credit or expensive stocks
trade_ideas.rationale: Wide valuation spreads, positive cash rates, and positioning that GMO expects to perform well in an AI unwind.
trade_ideas.risk: Management and operational risk, leveraging risk, and derivatives and short sales risk.

trade_ideas.description: Equity Dislocation: exploit the dislocation between value and growth stocks
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuation spreads between value and growth are wider than normal.

trade_ideas.description: Emerging FX: capture the cheapness of EM currencies
trade_ideas.rationale: GMO describes EM currencies as cheap.

risk_factors: Elevated risk of an unwind in the AI trade.
Management and operational risk: GMO's investment techniques may fail to produce desired results.
Leveraging risk from derivatives and securities lending.
Derivatives and short sales risk, including market, illiquidity, currency, credit and counterparty risk.
Mutual funds are more constrained in short and levered positions than hedge funds.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows equity valuation spreads wider than normal as of 9/30/2026. Percentile ranks listed include 95, 91, 96, 82, 90, 97, 94 and 76 across regional spreads, value vs. market and small value vs. market.

Exhibit 2 shows portfolio composition. Global Asset Allocation: Alternative Allocation 17.0%, Fixed Income 16.9%, Equities 62.2%, Cash 3.9%. Benchmark-Free Allocation: Alternative Allocation 13.1%, Equity Dislocation 14.6%, Fixed Income 26.6%, Emerging FX 1.9%, Equities 43.7%.
vol_and_positioning: ALTA is not designed as a tail-risk hedge (negative carry protection) but is managed for low correlation to equities.
ALTA's global macro exposure is net short equities.
ALTA allocation: 17.0% of Global Asset Allocation Strategy and 13.1% of Benchmark-Free Allocation Strategy as of 9/30/2026.
